The solution of puzzling issues such as the mass-generation mechanism, the lepton number violation, the absolute mass scale and the possible Majorana nature of neutrinos would open also new perspectives on baryogenesis and the evolution of the universe. In this respect, the observation of the rarest and elusive neutrinoless double $\beta $-decay process is expected to play a prominent role, so that its relevance can be hardly underestimated. In the present work, we fully reconstruct the genesis and the early history of double $\beta $-decay, starting from Maria Goeppert-Mayer's pioneering contribution, which promptly followed the first successful theory of $\beta $-decay provided by Enrico Fermi. Furthermore, we delve into Ettore Majorana's neutrino theory and a variety of related investigations, finally focusing on the neutrinoless version of double $\beta $-decay, whose existence was suggested by Wendell H. Furry in 1939 and put forward as a viable tool to discriminate between the very (Dirac or Majorana) nature of the electron neutrino.

arxiv:2610.33548.title: PeV Diffuse Neutrinos from Magnetically Arrested Disks in Low-Luminosity Active Galactic Nuclei
arxiv:2610.33548.abstract: Radiatively inefficient accretion flows (RIAFs) in low-luminosity active galactic nuclei (LLAGNs) are promising candidates for the PeV astrophysical diffuse neutrino background (DNB), but how the magnetically arrested disk (MAD) state affects their neutrino output and what fraction of LLAGNs are in this state remain unclear. We present a comprehensive study of diffuse neutrino emission from the inner accretion flows of LLAGNs in the MAD state, including all three flavors and both hadronuclear ($pp$) and photohadronic ($pγ$) production channels. Assuming that $\sim 5\%$ of the accretion power is transferred to nonthermal protons, current IceCube data allow at most $2.3\times10^{-3}$ of LLAGNs to have their inner accretion flows in a MAD state that can produce high-energy neutrinos. A lower fraction of the accretion power transferred to nonthermal protons would allow a proportionally larger fraction of such LLAGNs. Assuming that the comoving number density of low-excitation radio galaxies (LERGs) approximately matches that of LLAGNs in the MAD state, we also estimate a MAD fraction of $\simeq 1.6\times10^{-3}$. The corresponding diffuse intensity is compatible with current IceCube data and testable by IceCube-Gen2. For this MAD fraction, the all-flavor diffuse intensity peaks at $E_ν\simeq1.5\,{\rm PeV}$ with $E_ν^2Φ_ν\simeq2.6\times10^{-9}\,{\rm GeV\,cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}\,sr^{-1}}$. Current IceCube data are beginning to challenge several predictions from previous LLAGN RIAF models, and the MAD component can become the dominant contribution from LLAGN accretion flows beyond the cutoffs of most earlier RIAF spectra considered here.%%%This constraint suggests that only a small fraction of LLAGNs are supplied with sufficient coherent net poloidal magnetic flux.

arxiv:2610.33879.title: Finite-temperature ab-initio-Informed Nuclear Equation-of-State Tables (FINEST): Nuclear matter uncertainties in core-collapse supernovae
arxiv:2610.33879.abstract: We construct new finite-temperature, composition-dependent equation of state (EOS) tables for astrophysical simulations by implementing a recently developed energy-density functional. The functional is constrained by ab initio nuclear matter calculations and neutron-star observations. A distinguishing feature of this functional is a non-monotonic density dependence of the nucleon effective mass, with an increase beyond saturation density. Using these EOS tables, we investigate the impact of current uncertainties in nuclear matter properties on core-collapse supernova (CCSN) evolution with spherically symmetric simulations employing an effective treatment of convective mixing. The magnitude of the EOS effects depends on the progenitor compactness. Within current constraints, variations in incompressibility, symmetry energy, and high-density pressure produce only modest differences during the early post-bounce evolution. In contrast, the effective mass dependence has a much stronger influence on proto-neutron star contraction and the explosion dynamics in a stellar model with high core compactness. Its non-monotonic density dependence leads to a qualitatively different contraction history and can alter the explosion outcome compared to mean-field effective-mass behaviors. Therefore, among the nuclear matter properties considered, the density dependence of the nucleon effective masses has by far the largest impact on CCSN dynamics. This highlights the importance of realistic effective-mass parameterizations in nuclear EOSs used in astrophysical simulations.

arxiv:2610.33954.title: Core-Collapse Supernovae from Single and Binary-Stripped Massive Stars - I. Explodability and Nucleosynthesis
arxiv:2610.33954.abstract: Binary interaction can substantially alter massive-star evolution and pre-supernova structure, changing core-collapse outcomes and nucleosynthetic yields. We compare explodability and nucleosynthesis in 66 non-rotating, solar-metallicity single-star and binary-stripped progenitors spanning zero-age main-sequence (ZAMS) masses of $11$-$45\,{\rm M}_\odot$, using the spherically symmetric PUSH framework and nucleosynthesis post-processing. Both populations explode up to $22\,{\rm M}_\odot$, with binary stripping altering explodability at higher ZAMS masses. Successful explosions span similar energies ($\sim$0.4-1.3$\,$B) and remnant masses ($\sim$1.4-2.0$\,{\rm M}_\odot$). The largest nucleosynthetic differences occur at low ZAMS masses, particularly for material undergoing explosive O and Si burning. The $^{56}$Ni yields and iron-group abundances broadly agree with observations of core-collapse supernovae and the metal-poor star HD 84937. When compared with calculations using time-dependent mixing-length theory and a two-parameter explodability criterion for the same progenitors, our results reveal substantial differences in explodability, with agreement on successful explosions for only 5 cases across all three approaches. Nevertheless, elemental yield patterns can remain broadly similar for models that explode successfully across treatments. Salpeter initial-mass-function-weighted yields of most elements differ by $\sim$20% between populations, with K enhanced by a factor of $\sim$3.4 in the binary-stripped population, driven by increased production in the lowest-mass progenitors. Binary-stripped models show closer agreement with empirical core-collapse S, K, and Ca abundance ratios relative to Mg inferred from APOGEE, while Na remains overproduced in both populations. Together, our results highlight the need to account for binarity when interpreting supernova abundance patterns.

arxiv:2610.32619.title: Development of an Analog Front-End Using NINO ASIC for Mini-ICAL
arxiv:2610.32619.abstract: The mini-ICAL was supposed to be a pre-prototype detector of the Iron CALorimeter (ICAL) of the India-based Neutrino Observatory (INO) project. Resistive Plate Chamber (RPC) was the active element of these detectors. As this detector operates in avalanche mode, one needs a very fast pre-amplifier for signal processing. NINO ASIC developed for the ALICE time-of-flight detector was a potential chip to be used as the analog-front end. This paper presents an 8-in-1 pre-amplifier board developed using the NINO ASIC, a single-ended to differential signal conversion using the differential driver chip manufactured by Texas Instruments, production of the boards, lessons learned during production, testing of these boards, and interface with RPCs. Finally, its performance based on strip rates and efficiency of the detector will also be discussed.

arxiv:2610.35945.title: The SIRMOS mission concept: a space-based near-IR spectroscopic survey of 100 million galaxies in the Euclid Wide Survey footprint
arxiv:2610.35945.abstract: SIRMOS is a mission concept for a future NASA Astrophysics Explorer opportunity that aims to revolutionize our understanding of the universe by mapping the large-scale structure of galaxies in unprecedented breadth and detail to explore cosmic origins and evolution. Specifically, the primary science goals of SIRMOS are to discover how cosmic inflation seeded large-scale structure, reveal the nature of the accelerating expansion of the universe, and measure the sum of neutrino masses to exceptionally high precision. Its secondary science goals include determining how environment shapes galaxy evolution at cosmic noon and beyond, and probing the Milky Way's dust-enshrouded regions, reaching the far side of our Galaxy. To accomplish its transformative science goals, SIRMOS executes a 3-year cosmology survey over the Euclid footprint of ~14,000 deg$^2$, obtaining slit spectra for ~100 million galaxies at 1<z<4. SIRMOS is the first space mission designed specifically to leverage Euclid's wide near-infrared (IR) imaging survey for target selection and employs a digital micro-mirror device (DMD) to acquire up to 4,000 simultaneous spectra over a wide 0.9 deg$^2$ field of view. The instrument's excellent spectral resolution of $R=1300$ and continuous wavelength coverage from 1.25--2.5 $μ$m capture the redshifts of distant galaxies with no gaps, reducing systematic biases to achieve ground-breaking science.

arxiv:2610.30773.title: A Chiral Nelson-Barr Relaxion
arxiv:2610.30773.abstract: We present the chiral Nelson-Barr relaxion model, an extension of the Nelson-Barr relaxion framework with a gauged chiral $\mathrm{U}(1)$ symmetry. It includes vector-like quarks to cancel gauge anomalies and a scalar whose vacuum expectation value generates their masses. The chiral symmetry forbids the leading operators responsible for the Nelson-Barr and clockwork quality problems. Right-handed neutrinos generate light-neutrino masses through the type-I seesaw mechanism and permit thermal leptogenesis. For the particular coupling considered, relaxion phenomenology gives $f_{\mathrm{max}}^{\mathrm{pheno}}\sim 4\times 10^{11}\ \mathrm{GeV}$, about eight times the corresponding phenomenological ceiling in the original model. The model can accommodate thermal leptogenesis if its right-handed-neutrino masses and reheating history satisfy the required temperature bounds.

arxiv:2610.31666.title: Boosted Dark Matter Directionality in Large Liquid Scintillator Detectors
arxiv:2610.31666.abstract: Light dark matter can be boosted by cosmic-ray-dark matter interactions, which opens the possibility of direct-detection searches with large neutrino detectors. We consider the signal produced by boosted dark matter undergoing quasi-elastic scattering off carbon and knocking out a neutron in a large liquid scintillator detector. A distinctive delayed gamma ray from neutron capture can be reconstructed after $\sim 210$$μ$s, which is paired up with the prompt signal during neutron propagation. We find that 100 kt$\cdot$yr of data from the neutron-coincidence channel will be able to probe new parameter space compared to free proton signals found in previous work. We further consider the possibility of utilizing directional information from the displaced vertex associated with the capture of the final-state neutron. However, we find that directional information does not materially improve the sensitivity due to the large nucleon scattering angle.

arxiv:2610.31755.title: From Inspiral to Outburst: Modeling a Potential Luminous Red Nova from Betelgeuse
arxiv:2610.31755.abstract: Recent evidence suggests that Betelgeuse may host a stellar companion whose orbit will decay through tidal interactions, ultimately leading to engulfment and merger within the next several thousand years. If confirmed, this system could represent the nearest and best-characterized progenitor of a future luminous red nova (LRN). We investigate whether the shock-breakout and cooling emission preceding the LRN can be used to constrain the properties of the companion and its disruption within the stellar envelope. Using binary stellar evolution calculations, we evolve Betelgeuse with companions of $0.7$, $1.0$, and $2.0 M_\odot$ to the onset of common envelope evolution (CEE). We then perform one-dimensional radiation-hydrodynamic simulations that follow companion disruption, energy deposition, and shock propagation through the envelope. We find that the peak luminosity increases systematically with companion mass, from $2.44\times10^{41}$ to $6.17\times10^{41}$ erg s$^{-1}$ across the $0.7$-$2.0 M_\odot$ models, while the duration increases more modestly from $1.48$ to $1.99$ days and attains apparent magnitudes brighter than Venus as viewed from Earth. Tidal disruption contributes both kinetic energy and mass to the envelope, linking the companion's structure and mass to the energetics of the shock-heated ejecta. The monotonic luminosity sequence demonstrates that the early breakout emission can retain direct information about the engulfed companion. The interaction ejects $6.15$-$11.19 M_\odot$ of hydrogen-rich material, substantially modifying both the envelope structure and circumstellar environment prior to core collapse.

arxiv:2610.31758.title: Collapsars Are Not Heavy $r$-Process Factories
arxiv:2610.31758.abstract: Collapsar disks are proposed sources of $r$-process elements, but neutron-rich disk ejecta require gas to be both neutronized in the disk and ejected before accretion. The magnetic field that enables ejection also thickens the disk and accelerates the inflow, lowering both the density and the time available for weak processing. To compute the resulting neutronization, we evolve the electron fraction of the inflowing gas, adopting at each radius the temperature that maximizes the net neutronization rate for the local density and instantaneous composition. This yields a lower limit on $Y_{\rm e}$ that is independent of the disk's thermal history. We adopt an optimistic unbinding radius of $R_{\rm unb}=10\,r_g$ for all magnetic fluxes capable of launching outflows. Combining this ejection condition with favorable assumptions of low black hole mass, ejection of midplane gas, and the upper end of the $γ$-ray burst (GRB) engine-power scale, which limits the accretion rate to $\dot M_{\rm BH}\lesssim0.4\,M_\odot\,{\rm s}^{-1}$, gives a fiducial lower bound $Y_{\rm e}\gtrsim0.33$, above the characteristic $Y_{\rm e}\approx 0.25$ threshold for heavy $r$-process production. Stronger magnetic flux, toward which jet-launching engines evolve, raises the lower bound to $Y_{\rm e}\gtrsim0.49$. We conclude that collapsar disk outflows cannot supply the heavy $r$-process yields invoked for a dominant enrichment channel. Only engines with unusually high accretion rates, potentially including exceptionally luminous GRBs, such as GRB 221009A, and direct-horizon collapsars, may produce heavy $r$-process ejecta.

arxiv:2610.29942.title: PBR sensitivity to boosted dark matter explanation for the KM3-230213A event
arxiv:2610.29942.abstract: POEMMA-Balloon with Radio (PBR) is a hybrid fluorescence and optical Cherenkov telescope that is a pathfinder instrument for a future Probe Of Extreme Multi-Messenger Astrophysics (POEMMA), together with a radio instrument, to be flown on a super pressure balloon in Spring 2028. One of its science objectives is follow up of astrophysical event alerts via signals of tau decays in the atmosphere, sourced by Earth-skimming tau neutrinos. The recent report of the KM3NeT Collaboration's muon event with $ E_μ=120^{+110}_{-60}$ PeV sparked searches for beyond the standard model (BSM) physics explanations. Using a specific, boosted dark matter scenario which together with the KM3NeT observation, sets a scale for the fluence of boosted dark matter in this energy range, we assess the capabilities of PBR to constrain or discover such a source for a boosted dark matter energy spectrum above $\sim 10^8$ GeV. PBR has discovery potential for dark matter energies above $10^9$ GeV, and depending on BSM input parameters, to dark matter energies as low as $1.5\times 10^8$ GeV. While the analysis is focused on one BSM example, the methodology is applicable to any BSM physics that affects tau production in the Earth.

arxiv:2610.30240.title: Probing Heavy Neutral Leptons through New Gauge Interactions at the Forward Physics Facilities
arxiv:2610.30240.abstract: We investigate the prospects for improving the heavy neutral lepton (HNL) searches at the far-forward LHC experiments FASER and FASER$ν$, as well as their proposed HL-LHC successors, FASER2 and FASER$ν$2, using new HNL production mechanisms. We consider scenarios in which HNLs couple directly to a new $U(1)$ gauge boson and decay into visible Standard Model final states through mixing with active neutrinos. Focusing on the $U(1)_{B-L}$, $U(1)_{B-3L_τ}$, and $U(1)_B$ gauge extensions as benchmark models, we study HNL production through proton bremsstrahlung and Drell--Yan processes, which probe complementary mediator-mass regimes. We analyze several visible decay channels, including charged leptons, neutral mesons, and other hadrons, and evaluate the projected sensitivities for different neutrino-flavor mixing patterns. We find that these new production mechanisms that differ qualitatively from the conventional picture in which both production and decay are controlled by active-sterile mixing enable the far-forward LHC program to probe previously unexplored regions of HNL parameter space, with the first-ever demonstration of FASER$ν$ having sensitivity to HNLs and FASER2 and FASER$ν$2 offering substantially enhanced sensitivity during the HL-LHC era, even reaching the canonical seesaw prediction for all three lepton flavors. Our results demonstrate that new gauge interactions can substantially enhance HNL production independently of the active-sterile mixing that governs their visible decays, opening complementary opportunities to explore HNLs at the forward physics facilities.

arxiv:2610.30338.title: Machine Learning Neutrino-Nucleus Cross Sections II: More Leptons
arxiv:2610.30338.abstract: Neutrino-nucleus cross sections are essential inputs for long-baseline neutrino oscillation experiments, yet remain challenging to model with high precision. Recent work demonstrated that fully black-box data-driven cross-section models cannot accurately generalize between near- and far-detector fluxes, but imposing Standard-Model symmetries via structure-function parameterizations provides a well-posed learning problem in a simplified DUNE-inspired muon-neutrino disappearance analysis. Here, we extend this framework to multiple lepton flavors and both neutrino and antineutrino beam modes, incorporating the electron appearance channel and enabling a simultaneous determination of $\sin^2θ_{23}$, $Δm^2_{31}$, and the CP-violating phase $δ_{\rm CP}$. We find that the learned cross section model recovers the injected oscillation parameters without significant bias, with constraints comparable to those obtained using the exact underlying cross section. Flux uncertainties have more significant effects in the multi-channel case, and incorporating flux nuisance parameters into the learning problem is required for accurate results. Our results demonstrate that this data-driven approach can be extended to the multi-channel measurements needed for long-baseline neutrino oscillation analyses.

doi:10.1016/j.dark.2026.102496.title: Polarized emission, neutrino deposition and geodesic-induced quadrupole waveforms in exact Horndeski and disformal black-hole exteriors
doi:10.1016/j.dark.2026.102496.abstract: We study which observables retain information about the radial structure of exact black-hole exteriors when circular-orbit or shadow diagnostics are degenerate. We compare the static non-stealth seed of quartic square-root Horndeski theory and a separate constant-kinetic disformal exterior. The first metric is used in its original seed frame, not as a new disformally generated solution. The specified nonzero-hair square-root realization has a horizon-divergent scalar invariant and an exterior scalar ghost with a negative radial characteristic speed squared. For the inverse-square lapse N = 1 − 2 M / r − χ M 2 / r 2 , we derive an exact eccentric separatrix and regular anomaly equations. At fixed turning points (8M, 24M), changing χ from zero to one lowers the radial frequency by 5.18% and raises the azimuthal frequency by 6.53%, although a different Schwarzschild orbit can match both frequencies. Fully differentiated eccentric mass quadrupoles yield distinct numerical-kludge burst profiles and, for suitable periodicity classes, a recurrence shorter than orbital closure. These are geodesic-induced quadrupole waveforms. Polarization is a source-dependent geometric response, and moving the prescribed neutrinosphere can reverse the fixed-radius deposition trend. The constant-disformal comparison preserves the critical shadow radius and azimuthal frequency while changing radial and transport observables. Published EHT and stellar-precession summaries are translated only into approximate, assumption-dependent consistency estimates. In particular, a Gaussian summary likelihood with a uniform nonnegative-χ prior gives approximate 95% upper endpoints 0.967 and 1.142 for the two Sgr A* mass–distance priors. Fixed-theory mass comparisons retain the coupling length.

doi:10.1007/s41365-026-02048-4.title: Rejection of pile-up events in Li$_{2}$MoO$_{4}$ scintillating bolometers for neutrinoless double-beta decay detection
doi:10.1007/s41365-026-02048-4.abstract:
Neutrinoless double-beta decay (0$
u  eta  eta$) detection necessitates an exceptionally low background, as this hypothesized process has not been observed; current experimental lower limits on its half-life are of order $10^{26}$ years. When the intrinsic background from the detector and its passive support materials is low, the primary sources of this background in 0$
u  eta  eta$ experiments of $^{100}$Mo are the pile-up events of two-neutrino double-beta decay events and alpha events. This work presents methods that contribute to further reducing pile-up events, thereby supporting the feasibility of 0$
u  eta  eta$ detection. One is a time-over-threshold (TOT) method, wherein the amplitude of the signal is compared against a threshold, and the duration of the signal exceeding the threshold is measured. This method aims to discern pile-up events by analyzing the time duration discrepancy between pile-up events and single events of equivalent amplitude. Using MATLAB, the double-exponential ideal waveform is first generated, followed by the addition of white Gaussian noise to simulate realistic signal conditions. The method is evaluated in two scenarios: a constant threshold and a dynamically changing threshold. Compared with a constant threshold, a dynamic threshold that adjusts according to the waveform can effectively improve discrimination efficiency. The results demonstrate that the TOT method with a dynamically changing threshold reaches a discrimination efficiency of 92.5% at a signal-to-noise ratio of 30, and that at higher signal-to-noise ratios its efficiency is comparable to that of the traditional mean-time method. This paper also attempts to improve the mean-time method, including the generalization of the mean-time definition and its combination with the TOT method. Moreover, in this paper, calculations of the achievable background index for projected light detectors under different rise times and signal-to-noise ratios are performed. In an actual experiment, the background index is influenced by various factors beyond the simulation work. Nevertheless, the background suppression scheme proposed in this work provides a solid foundation for the next-generation CUPID experiment to achieve the physics goal, reducing the background index below $1	imes 10^{-4}$ counts/(keV$\cdot$kg$\cdot$yr).

doi:10.22323/1.523.0018.title: Data and Computing Infrastructure for KM3NeT- Towards Full Deployment
doi:10.22323/1.523.0018.abstract: The KM3NeT Collaboration is building two Cherenkov neutrino detectors in the depths of the Mediterranean Sea to study both the intrinsic properties of neutrinos and cosmic high-energy neutrino sources. For the detection of Cherenkov light generated by charged particles from neutrino induced interactions the detectors share the same technology of large arrays of optical modules. The expected data volume grows roughly linearly with the number of optical modules, reaching hundreds of terabytes per year at full deployment. To handle this load, a Rucio file catalogue will manage distributed data storage and replication, and the DIRAC workload manager will orchestrate large-scale data processing and Monte Carlo simulations. This infrastructure allows the collaboration to scale efficiently with detector size while supporting real-time data acquisition, processing, and analysis workflows. This contribution focuses on the KM3NeT data and computing infrastructure, describing the current computing model and its evolution toward distributed Grid-based resources as the experiment approaches full deployment.

arxiv:2610.28482.title: The "Rubin 2036: Opportunities for Discovery" Workshop: A Community Roadmap for the Future of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory After the LSST
arxiv:2610.28482.abstract: The NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory will complete its ten-year Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) in the mid-2030s. Its 8.4 m aperture and 9.6 square degree field of view give it an étendue unmatched by any facility planned for that era. The Rubin 2036: Opportunities for Discovery workshop (KIPAC/SLAC, 3-5 August 2026) brought together approximately 100 participants to discuss Rubin's future after LSST. This paper summarizes the workshop's structure and discussions across five working groups. The continued-surveying group explored a machine-learning foundation model pretrained on Rubin imaging for detection, deblending, and classification. The cadence group considered allocating post-LSST observing time and strategies for transiting exoplanets, Type Ia supernova cosmology, time-delay cosmography, and second-scale transients. The filter group explored broadband, medium-band, and narrowband filters for photometric redshifts, high-redshift large-scale structure, AGN reverberation mapping, Galactic archaeology, and emission-line imaging. The multi-messenger group explored follow-up of next-generation gravitational-wave and neutrino sources, including standard sirens, kilonovae, and Galactic supernovae. The technology group organized options by cost and lead time, including fast readout, new filters, a faster shutter, and summit edge computing. Cross-cutting topics included AI/ML, Chilean and Latin-American co-leadership, satellite megaconstellations, and weather and climate trends at Cerro Pachón. White papers and workshop talks are available through https://zenodo.org/communities/rubin2036workshop/ and https://rubin-observatory.github.io/Rubin-Beyond-LSST/pages/Rubin2036proceedings/.

arxiv:2610.28744.title: The renormalization-group running of neutrino mixing is undetectable
arxiv:2610.28744.abstract: Quantum corrections make the parameters of a theory depend on an arbitrary renormalization scale, $μ$. The renormalization-group (RG) running of neutrino masses and mixing is a standard tool to relate models defined at a high mass scale to measured values. A growing body of work holds that the running is also directly observable: a neutrino produced or detected at momentum transfer $Q$ would carry the mixing matrix evaluated at $μ= Q$. Proposed signatures include flavor change at zero distance from the source, shifts in the measured CP-violation phase, and an anomalous flavor composition of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos. We show that this premise is incorrect. The mixing is a property of the neutrino itself, fixed by its self-energy on the mass shell, not by the process that produces or detects it. Setting $μ= Q$ is legitimate, but then large logarithms in the self-energy undo the running; the premise incorrectly drops them. Hence, apart from small vertex and box corrections, every experiment measures the same mixing: the running is undetectable. We illustrate this in the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model, two seesaw models, and the Standard Model effective field theory. Independently, short-baseline data already limit the change of any one mixing angle between pion decay and detection at $Q$ of a few GeV to below $0.7^\circ$--$2.4^\circ$.

doi:10.1134/s1062873826701893.title: Baksan Large Neutrino Telescope: Project Development and Infrastructure Design
doi:10.1134/s1062873826701893.abstract: The current status of the Baksan Large Neutrino Telescope project is presented in this work. The results of the first stage-a prototype with a target mass of 0.5 t-were described. The main improvements in the second prototype were also outlined: the magnetic field compensation system and the liquid scintillator purification system.

doi:10.1134/s1062873826701881.title: Multipurpose Compact Neutrino Detector Based on a Gadolinium-Gallium-Containing Scintillator
doi:10.1134/s1062873826701881.abstract: A concept of a multipurpose compact neutrino detector based on GAGG:Ce crystals is proposed. Its potential applications include testing the gallium anomaly using artificial neutrino sources, searching for 2νββ and 0νββ decays of the $^{160}$Gd isotope, as well as detecting solar neutrinos. A prototype of a unit cell for such a detector is presented.

arxiv:2610.25214.title: Lorentz-Invariance Violation with neutrinos from gamma-ray bursts using IceCube High-Energy Starting Events 12-year dataset
arxiv:2610.25214.abstract: High-energy astrophysical neutrinos provide a unique probe of Lorentz-invariance violation (LIV), as small energy-dependent deviations from the speed of light can produce measurable time delays over cosmological distances. We search for LIV-induced correlations between neutrinos and gamma-ray bursts using the public 12-year IceCube High-Energy Starting Event dataset and a catalog of 746 bursts with measured redshifts. We develop a likelihood analysis accounting for neutrino directional and energy uncertainties, a possible intrinsic time offset between neutrino and gamma-ray emission, and the decay of superluminal neutrinos expected within effective field theory. For linear LIV, the data show a mild preference over the background-only hypothesis, with a $p$-value of $3.1\%$, corresponding to a one-sided Gaussian significance of approximately $1.9σ$. The best fit corresponds to a LIV scale $Λ_{\rm LIV}=5.8\times10^{17}\,\mathrm{GeV}$ and is effectively driven by the subluminal component, as superluminal neutrinos are strongly suppressed by LIV-induced decays at the analyzed energies. The preferred LIV scale and the most significant neutrino--gamma-ray burst associations are consistent with previous studies based on different statistical approaches. No evidence for quadratic LIV is found. These results motivate further searches with complementary neutrino datasets, particularly at lower energies, where the superluminal component may become observable.

arxiv:2610.21886.title: Low-Scale See-Saw Mechanism and the Majorana Nature of Heavy Neutrinos
arxiv:2610.21886.abstract: We investigate the possibility to determine the Majorana nature of the heavy Majorana neutrinos present in the low-scale type I seesaw mechanism of neutrino mass generation in experiments at $e^+ \text{-} e^-$ and $μ^+ \text{-} μ^-$ colliders. This is done on the examples of two specific symmetry-protected seesaw scenarios with two right-handed (RH) singlet neutrinos and one seesaw realization with three RH neutrinos. We use the forward-backward symmetry in the angular distribution of the heavy neutral leptons produced in the $e^+ \text{-} e^-$ and $μ^+ \text{-} μ^-$ collisions as an indicator of their Majorana nature. Our results indicate that the experiments at FCCee during its first phase of operation have a remarkable potential not only to discover the heavy neutral leptons associated with the type I seesaw mechanism if they have masses smaller than the $Z^0$-boson mass, but also to probe and provide evidence for their Majorana nature.

doi:10.1007/s10751-026-02800-7.title: Energy loss and quenching-factor studies for low-recoil collision cascades in silicon using molecular dynamics simulations
doi:10.1007/s10751-026-02800-7.abstract: Low-energy nuclear recoils in semiconductor detectors like Silicon (Si) and Germanium (Ge), play a crucial role in direct Dark-Matter detection and coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CE$\nu$NS) experiments. In this preliminary work, we employ classical molecular dynamics simulations to investigate energy-partitioning processes in crystalline silicon for recoil energies ranging from 20 eV to 10 keV. Silicon primary knock-on atoms (PKAs) were initiated within a $(20 \times 20 \times 20)\,\text { \text{\AA }}^{3}$ Silicon supercell using periodic diamond-cubic lattice, and the resulting collision cascades were analyzed using molecular dynamics framework together with an energy-dependent electronic stopping derived from SRIM calculations. The partitioning of recoil energy between atomic motion and electronic energy dissipation was quantified, and quenching factors (QFs) were estimated from the cumulative electronic energy loss. The calculated QF values exhibit systematic deviations from the Lindhard's model in the sub-10 keV regime, indicating a reduced electronic-energy fraction for low-energy recoils. Comparison with available experimental data shows overall qualitative agreement across the investigated energy range. The preliminary results of this study demonstrate the potential of atomistic molecular dynamics simulations to provide microscopic insight into low-energy recoil processes and detector response in silicon-based rare-event searches. Further simulations, analysis and studies are going on to get much deeper understanding of the findings.

doi:10.1103/bk55-z2mq.title: Toward measuring the low-energy cosmic-ray spectrum with next-generation neutrino detectors
doi:10.1103/bk55-z2mq.abstract: We investigate the capabilities of upcoming kiloton-scale neutrino detectors, such as Hyper-Kamiokande, in determining the primary cosmic-ray spectrum. These detectors provide full-sky coverage and long-term monitoring, unlike traditional satellite and balloon experiments that measure cosmic-ray flux at specific altitudes and locations. By analyzing the atmospheric neutrino flux generated by cosmic-ray interactions, we demonstrate that future detectors can differentiate between various cosmic-ray models with high statistical significance, even when accounting for uncertainties in neutrino cross sections and hadronic interactions. We introduce a technique for reconstructing the primary cosmic-ray spectrum using neutrino measurements, which reduces the flux uncertainty from approximately 20% to about 7%. We then show that Hyper-K has the potential to increase sensitivity to neutrino oscillation parameters, such as sin 2 θ 23 , by a factor of 2. Our results highlight the complementary role of neutrino detectors in cosmic-ray physics and their critical importance for precision measurements in particle astrophysics.

arxiv:2610.20163.title: Search for High-Energy Neutrinos from Infrared Flares
arxiv:2610.20163.abstract: IceCube has detected a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos. While its astrophysical origin is unknown, a significant neutrino emission has been observed from the gamma-ray blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Seyfert galaxy NGC 1068. This suggests accretion by supermassive black holes as one of the candidate mechanisms of the diffuse neutrino flux. Indeed, external studies that made use of IceCube data identified candidate sources, including AT2019dsg, likely a stellar tidal disruption event (TDE), and AT2019fdr, associated with an active galactic nucleus (AGN). An additional study using an optically detected sample of 63 accretion flares revealed another candidate as a potential high-energy neutrino counterpart: AT2019aalc. All of these candidate transients exhibit strong dust echoes, characterized by delayed infrared (IR) emission relative to the initial optical outburst. We look for correlations between the most comprehensive catalog of infrared flares and 10 years of IceCube archival data. We perform a time-dependent stacking analysis testing 393 sources in the Northern Sky against 10 years of through-going tracks. No significant neutrino emission is observed, and we derive upper limits to constrain neutrino emission from this catalog. These limits are subsequently extrapolated to a population-level study. We find that the contribution of IR flares to the IceCube diffuse neutrino flux at 100 TeV is below 2.7% for a spectral index of 2.5.

arxiv:2610.18223.title: Cryogenic characterisation of the FBK NUV-HD-cryo Silicon Photomultipliers for the DarkSide-20k dark matter experiment
arxiv:2610.18223.abstract: Liquid Argon Time Projection Chambers (TPCs) are highly promising detectors for dark matter searches due to their uniform response, scalability to large target masses, and compatibility with ultra-low background conditions. The DarkSide-20k (DS-20k) experiment, currently under construction at Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare (INFN) Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso (LNGS), aims to achieve unprecedented sensitivity to Weakly Interacting Massive Particles (WIMPs), approaching the neutrino fog. At the heart of the detector is a dual-phase TPC filled and surrounded by low-radioactivity argon from underground sources (i.e. Underground Argon (UAr)), functioning both as the WIMP target and detection medium. The experiment employs Fondazione Bruno Kessler (FBK) NUV-HD-cryo Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs) as the chosen photon sensors for its optical planes. Key SiPM properties such as dark noise rate, gain and direct crosstalk were measured using specialized test setups at 77 K. The photon detection efficiency (PDE) was measured under vacuum at 77 K over the wavelength range 350-820 nm. Secondary photon emission, which can give rise to external optical crosstalk, was measured under vacuum at 86 K over the wavelength range 550-1020 nm.

doi:10.1103/kjkf-x79r.title: Neutrino flux from collisions of red giant cores in globular clusters
doi:10.1103/kjkf-x79r.abstract: The coalescence of degenerate helium cores during red giant collisions—a process we term “erythrohenosis”—introduces a novel class of transient astrophysical sources of high-energy neutrinos. Using stellar models generated with mesa and smoothed-particle hydrodynamics simulations of the final inspiral phase, we develop a semianalytical model to estimate the amount of hydrogen mixed into the cores, the energy release ( ≈ 4.28 × 10 49 erg ) that heats the remnant to T f ≈ 5.3 × 10 8 K , the magnetic field amplification ( B ≈ 1.77 × 10 10 G ), and the resulting neutrino flux. The predicted TeV–PeV neutrino signal may contribute to the diffuse IceCube neutrino flux; we estimate that the horizon at which a single neutrino event is expected on average at ≳ 100 TeV is ≈ 55 kpc for individual merger events. Furthermore, we discuss the probability of a magnetized helium flash and assess the subsequent activation of the CNO cycle in the remnant core due to hydrogen mixing. In particular, neutrinos from the decay of F 18 offer a direct observational test of the detonation, (as sources within ∼ 4.4 pc would produce a neutrino flux exceeding the solar CNO neutrino background). The simultaneous emission of high-energy hadronic neutrinos, gravitational waves, and—if the optical depth permits ( τ T ∼ 10 14 in the core of the remnant)—an electromagnetic signal would constitute a unique multimessenger signature of red giant core collisions, positioning erythrohenosis events as exotic yet potentially observable phenomena in dense stellar systems.

doi:10.1140/epjp/s13360-026-08391-0.title: Observational constraints on Rényi holographic dark energy with massive neutrinos from DESI DR2, Planck, and supernovae
doi:10.1140/epjp/s13360-026-08391-0.abstract:
We investigate the Rényi holographic dark energy (RHDE) model with the Hubble horizon as the infrared cutoff, confronting it with DESI DR2 BAO, Planck 2018 CMB (both distance priors and, for one combination, the full TTTEEE+lensing likelihood), cosmic chronometers, and three supernova samples (Pantheon+SH0ES, Union3, and DES-SN5Y). The RHDE model yields $H_0 \simeq 69.9$-$70.2\ 	ext {km}\,	ext {s}^{-1}\,	ext {Mpc}^{-1}$, reducing the SH0ES tension from $>5\sigma$ to $\sim 2.3\sigma$-$2.6\sigma$. A strong negative $\delta$-$H_0$ degeneracy ($r \approx -0.9$) indicates that much of this reduction is statistical rather than a pure physical effect. The neutrino mass bound is $\Sigma m_
u < 0.27$-$0.31\ 	ext {eV}$ (95% CL) using CMB distance priors, and $\Sigma m_
u < 0.41\ 	ext {eV}$ when the full Planck likelihood is employed; a weak $\delta$-$\Sigma m_
u$ correlation ($r \approx -0.15$) confirms that the constraint is data-driven. AIC and BIC favour RHDE when supernova data are included. Separate early- and late-Universe analyses agree below $2.5\sigma$, demonstrating the model's coherence across cosmic epochs.

arxiv:2610.16968.title: Self-Interacting Dark Matter: From Particle Physics Theories to Structure Formation Simulations
arxiv:2610.16968.abstract: We establish a unified theory-to-simulation framework for self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) that integrates three components: (i) a comprehensive, self-contained treatment of its particle-physics foundations and a broad range of model classes; (ii) a systematic, quantitative mapping from microscopic dark-sector physics to structure-formation simulation inputs through explicit expressions and numerical prescriptions; and (iii) the development, implementation, and validation of a broad suite of SIDM algorithms and a dedicated DM decay module in the moving-mesh code AREPO-2. Under (i), we detail the particle content, symmetries, interactions, production mechanisms, and constraints of a broad landscape of elementary and composite SIDM models, and present representative viable benchmark models. Under (ii), the mapping specifies cosmological initial conditions, internal-state masses and populations, reaction networks, velocity- and angle-dependent cross sections, dissipative energy loss, and decay rates and recoil kinematics. We then apply this mapping to a broad range of SIDM model classes. Under (iii), we implement and validate SIDM algorithms with constant and velocity-dependent cross sections, covering isotropic and anisotropic scattering, multi-state elastic and inelastic reactions, and dissipative processes, alongside a dedicated DM decay module in AREPO-2. We validate these implementations through beam-lattice deflection experiments, thermalization and uniform-box decay tests, isolated-halo gravothermal core-collapse simulations, and cosmological box and zoom-in simulations. These tests recover analytical predictions, establish agreement across numerical schemes, and reproduce published benchmarks. Our theory-to-simulation framework serves as a cross-disciplinary reference and a practical bridge between SIDM particle physics and simulations of nonlinear structure formation.

arxiv:2610.13930.title: The LZ inelastic splitting as a probe of anomaly mediation
arxiv:2610.13930.abstract: The LZ 248 keV recoil candidate admits an interpretation in terms of pseudo-Dirac dark matter with a mixing-suppressed inelastic $Z$ interaction. In the MSSM, the Higgsino limit conflicts with the adopted solar-neutrino bound, while a gaugino realization requires an unprotected mass degeneracy. We realize such spectra in the MRSSM, where an $R$-symmetric Dirac bino produces the required $Z$ transition and wino coannihilation supplies the observed relic abundance. We impose the Higgs and gauge coupling relations of $N=2$ supersymmetry at a high scale and evolve them to low energy. With the remaining model parameters held fixed, we obtain spectra spanning roughly 300-850 GeV that satisfy the adopted constraints and have a small diagonal axial current. If anomaly mediation dominates the Majorana splitting, its local scale is tens of MeV for splittings of a few hundred keV. A five-dimensional warped construction generates this scale through Goldberger-Wise stabilization and a loop correction to the no-scale Kähler potential. The spectra remain testable through elastic scattering, solar neutrinos and long-lived charged states.

arxiv:2610.14144.title: Planck-Scale Constraints on Quantum Gravity-Induced Neutrino Decoherence with IceCube
arxiv:2610.14144.abstract: Many quantum gravity theories predict spacetime fluctuations at the Planck scale. Neutrinos, which interact only via the weak force and gravity, propagate over long distances without losing quantum coherence. Planck-scale fluctuations would spoil that coherence, damping the flavor oscillation probability over long baselines. This makes neutrinos sensitive interferometers for Planck-scale physics. We present a search for quantum decoherence using 368,071 atmospheric neutrinos detected by IceCube in the energy range 0.5-100 TeV, an order of magnitude higher in energy than any previous decoherence search. We find no evidence for decoherence and set the strongest constraints to date on this class of neutrino decoherence models, improving on previous limits by over an order of magnitude for decoherence rate scaling as $E^2$ and $E^3$. These results exclude natural Planck-suppressed decoherence for all energy scalings $E^n$ with $0\leq n \leq 3$, the first such exclusion at the Planck scale for $n=3$.

arxiv:2610.14178.title: Collider and direct detection as key probes of asymmetric dark matter: Signals from a compressed Inert Higgs doublet
arxiv:2610.14178.abstract: The cosmic imbalance of particles over antiparticles may be inherited by the dark matter in a certain class of asymmetric dark matter models. In this article, we thoroughly investigate the signatures of the minimal realization of this idea. In this model a new (stable) inert Higgs, $H'$, plays the role of the mediator that facilitates the asymmetry transfer from the visible to the dark sector. It also constitutes a small dark matter sub-component, while the dominant component stems from a singlet scalar asymmetry. A combination of phenomenological and cosmological constraints requires this new inert Higgs doublet to be quite light $46\,{\rm GeV}<m_{H'}< 580\,{\rm GeV}$ and its spectrum rather compressed, $ΔM = m_{H^\pm}-m_{H_0} \lesssim 1\,{\rm GeV}$ and $δm = m_{A_0}-m_{H_0}\lesssim 5\,{\rm MeV}$. Therefore its charged component can be relatively long-lived on collider length-scales. By recasting searches for compressed Higgsinos at the LHC, we derive new limits on this particle and show that, while at present most of the parameter space for this state is still unconstrained, large and key regions of parameter space will be tested at the HL-LHC by a combination of searches for disappearing charged tracks and displaced soft tracks. Quite remarkably, the lifetime of the charged component of the doublet can be correlated with the dark matter interaction rate at direct detection experiments and we show that the next generation of direct detection experiments has a unique sensitivity to the parameter space in the model. The fact that a small neutral mass splitting is a prediction of the asymmetric setup makes it an interesting candidate to account for the high energy nuclear recoil event recently reported by the LZ experiment. More generally, our detailed phenomenological study holds for any dark matter model involving an inert Higgs doublet with mass below 580 GeV.

arxiv:2610.11839.title: Searching for Charged Lepton Flavor Violation
arxiv:2610.11839.abstract: Searches for Charged Lepton Flavor Violation (CLFV) are powerful tools to probe physics beyond the Standard Model (BSM). This chapter provides a comprehensive survey of CLFV theory, focusing primarily on low-energy muon and tau transitions while outlining complementary searches from high-energy colliders. Grounded in the Effective Field Theory (EFT) framework, we systematically review key observables including radiative and purely leptonic decays of muon and tau as well as $μ\to e$ conversion in nuclei and $τ$ hadronic decay channels. CLFV involving light new physics particles is also discussed. This review captures the modern synergy between EFTs, novel light-mediator scenarios, and hadronic and nuclear physics in the ongoing hunt for BSM signals.

arxiv:2610.09748.title: Cosmic Birefringence from Large Lepton Asymmetry
arxiv:2610.09748.abstract: Cosmic birefringence, the rotation of the polarization plane of cosmic microwave background (CMB) photons, provides an intriguing probe of physics beyond the Standard Model. In this paper, we investigate a vector Chern-Simons coupling between the neutrino current and photons as a possible origin of isotropic cosmic birefringence. Firstly, we perform the first analysis of anisotropic cosmic birefringence induced by the neutrino current. We find that the anisotropic signal sourced by lepton-number isocurvature fluctuations can be important on large scales, whereas on small scales, the anisotropic signal induced by gravitational effects becomes dominant comparing with the axion-like particle (ALP) scenario. Secondly, we show that a large lepton asymmetry generated through the Affleck-Dine mechanism can successfully account for the observed isotropic birefringence, and discuss its possible connection to the recently reported low helium-4 abundances in Subaru EMPRESS and Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT).

arxiv:2610.08139.title: The neutrino magnetic moment and supernovae with strong magnetic fields
arxiv:2610.08139.abstract: Despite several decades of searches, the neutrino magnetic moment remains unknown. If it is large, the neutrino evolution can be affected by its coupling to strong magnetic fields like the ones present in at least some core-collapse supernovae. We explore these effects for Majorana neutrinos. We first discuss a schematic model often employed and show the impact of resonant spin-flavor precession on the neutrino signal for a future galactic supernova. Then, we consider detailed simulations of a neutrino-driven supernova with 17 ${\rm M}_{\odot}$ leaving a neutron star and a magnetorotational supernova with 26 ${\rm M}_{\odot}$ with a black-hole remnant. We present predictions for the supernova neutrino fluxes and the event rates in presence of a non-zero neutrino magnetic moment, for the running JUNO and upcoming Hyper-Kamiokande experiments. Our results show a significant impact for transition magnetic moments of $10^{-14} ~μ_B$ during the neutronization burst and the accretion phase for the neutrino driven supernova, and as small as $10^{-15} ~μ_B$ at the early times for the magnetorotational supernova.

doi:10.1016/j.newast.2026.102662.title: Classical long gamma-ray bursts as multimessenger sources: Recent developments in gamma-rays, neutrinos, and cosmic rays
doi:10.1016/j.newast.2026.102662.abstract: The status of classical high-luminosity long gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) as candidate sources of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs) and high-energy neutrinos has changed substantially since 2019, and it has changed on three fronts more or less simultaneously. We restrict attention to that population throughout; the low-luminosity and hidden populations, on which the recent constraints bear far more weakly, are discussed only where recent results bear on them. A very-high-energy (VHE, E ≳ 100 GeV) class of GRBs has been established by H.E.S.S., MAGIC, and LHAASO, culminating in GRB 221009A, for which the onset of the TeV afterglow was resolved and photons up to ∼ 13 TeV were recorded. IceCube has converted the absence of GRB neutrinos into quantitative bounds, both through stacked searches over thousands of bursts and through burst-specific limits on GRB 221009A. The Pierre Auger Observatory and the Telescope Array have consolidated a mass composition that grows heavier above the ankle, with a narrowing X max dispersion, and Auger has reported evidence, at the ∼ 4 σ level, for an intermediate-scale anisotropy towards the Centaurus region, compatible with several nearby galaxy catalogues including starbursts. This focus review covers these developments and the constraints they place on one another, rather than the GRB field as a whole. These constraints apply to physically distinct regions: the TeV photons are afterglow emission from the external forward shock, whereas the neutrino limits and the Fermi-LAT cascade bound constrain the prompt dissipation zone, and the site of nuclear acceleration and escape is a model assumption in both cases. We therefore map each constraint onto its zone before combining anything. Within a single zone the compactness that governs photomeson production also governs photodisintegration and internal γ γ opacity, so transparency, neutrino faintness and nuclear survival are not independent; across zones no such implication holds without a model linking the prompt and afterglow flows. What the recent measurements do show is a convergence: analyses of different zones, by different methods, favour the same corner of parameter space, namely large radii and high bulk Lorentz factors, with the prompt-zone limits additionally requiring low baryonic loading. We summarize the resulting picture, which applies to co-spatial one-zone models of classical long GRBs and leaves multi-zone, reverse-shock, low-luminosity, and choked-jet configurations largely untested, together with the systematic uncertainties that currently limit it and the observations with CTAO, IceCube-Gen2, KM3NeT, GRAND, and AugerPrime that would test it. •Each recent gamma-ray, neutrino and cosmic-ray limit is mapped to its emission zone.•Independent constraints on distinct zones converge on high Γ and thin photon fields.•One-zone classical long-GRB models survive only at high Γ and large radii.•Multi-zone, low-luminosity and hidden-jet routes remain largely untested.

doi:10.1103/rm1g-qtk7.title: Observing micro-black-hole dark matter
doi:10.1103/rm1g-qtk7.abstract: Primordial micro black holes can constitute dark matter if short-distance gravity is modified by extra dimensions or a large number of species and if the memory-burden effect sufficiently suppresses Hawking evaporation. The resulting black holes in the transition regime differ from their four-dimensional Einsteinian counterparts through their mass—radius relation, temperature, entropy, and lifetime, which can render even very light objects cosmologically stable. The most promising observational consequences of such micro black hole dark matter are analyzed. Neutron star survival yields the most robust constraints, while a narrow region of parameter space can simultaneously remain viable and address the missing-pulsar problem in the Galactic Center. Diffuse evaporation signals in neutrino telescopes are found to be relevant mainly in extradimensional scenarios, whereas in generic species models, visible emission is strongly suppressed by evaporation into dark sectors. Merger-induced evaporation bursts can provide an additional probe in extradimensional realizations if the postmerger remnant briefly returns to the semiclassical phase. Overall, micro-black-hole dark matter remains phenomenologically viable in constrained regions, with neutron stars, neutrino telescopes, and merger signatures providing complementary tests.

inspire:3220639.title: Pati–Salam Landscape from Intersecting D-Branes
inspire:3220639.abstract: The monograph provides a complete enumeration of the three-family supersymmetric Pati–Salam landscape from intersecting D6-branes, identifying 33 independent models with distinct gauge coupling relations at the string scale. A detailed phenomenological analysis reduces these to 17 models with viable Yukawa structures capable of accommodating the observed fermion masses, neutrino masses, and flavor mixing. The viable models organize into four classes distinguished by their Higgs content, with the 12-Higgs class providing a particularly distinctive realization of Dirac neutrino masses consistent with phenomenological and swampland constraints. The book further derives the supersymmetry-breaking soft terms across the viable landscape and reveals how their dependence on D6-brane geometry differs from that of the Yukawa couplings, providing a direct link between the internal string geometry and low-energy phenomenology.

arxiv:2610.04909.title: The Phenomenology of the Dark Dimension and Non-Supersymmetric Strings
arxiv:2610.04909.abstract: Swampland principles, combined with the smallness of dark energy $Λ$, lead to the dark dimension scenario, with one extra dimension of micron size. We review this scenario and its predictions: KK graviton dark matter (or the KK tower of the quintessence field into which the gravitons convert), neutrino masses tied to $Λ^{1/4}$ via a bulk $B-L$ gauge symmetry, QCD axion decay constant $f_a\sim Λ^{1/12}\sim 10^9-10^{10}$ GeV at the 5d Planck scale $M_5$, connecting electroweak hierarchy to $Λ^{1/6}$, and a relation between the GUT and weak scales with $M_5$ as the geometric mean. The dark dimension also provides a concrete realization of an evolving dark sector: the evolution of its diameter correlates the variation of dark energy with that of the dark matter mass, fitting the recent DESI DR2 (+CMB+supernovae) data while avoiding the phantom crossing that the $w_0w_a$CDM parametrization would suggest---the apparent phantom behavior instead arises from the evolving dark matter mass. The fits suggest that the dark energy field sits in the interior of moduli space, near an unstable critical point. Motivated by this, we review recent progress on non-supersymmetric string vacua: isolated critical points protected by duality symmetries, in non-geometric flux compactifications and in Scherk--Schwarz compactifications of M-theory, and an emerging duality web for non-supersymmetric strings. This note is based on two talks given by the author at String Phenomenology 2026 (Paris) and Strings 2026 (Shanghai).

inspire:3220873.title: Primordial high energy neutrino and non-abelian dark matter: phenomenology of early Universe relics
inspire:3220873.abstract: The Standard Model of particle physics and the ΛCDM model of cosmology account for aremarkable range of observations, yet they remain incomplete. This thesis studies relics of theearly Universe, particles produced when in its early stages, in two different regimes: stablerelics which are still around today that could explain the dark matter problem, and unstablerelics which have decayed long ago and of which the products could allow us to probe theearly Universe.The first part considers unstable relics, and in particular asks whether decays into neutrinoscould lead to observable signatures today. Neutrinos are the only Standard Model particlesable to reach us from before recombination, and neutrino telescopes routinely detect themat high energies, so that a sufficiently energetic primordial injection could be visible today.We call such a neutrino a Phenu, for primordial high energy neutrino. We derive the Phenuspectra expected at Earth today for several types of sharp spectral features that a decayingor annihilating relic could produce, and delineate the region of the relic mass, lifetime andabundance for which the Phenu could propagate unimpeded until today. Confronting thisregion with the constraints from cosmology and already observed fluxes, we determine theregion of the parameter space for which such a signal could be observed in existing andfuture neutrino telescopes. To study the complementary region, in which distortions due tointeractions are expected, we develop a Monte Carlo code which follows the propagation ofPhenus, and apply it to the KM3NeT ultrahigh energy event, the most energetic neutrinoever detected to date. We show that a primordial origin can better accommodate the eventthan a single power law, and help alleviate part of the tension with the non-observations ofsimilar events at IceCube and Auger.The second part considers relics which are present today: dark matter particles. Wepresent a mechanism in which the stability of scalar dark matter follows from the centre of anon-abelian dark gauge group rather than from an ad-hoc symmetry. We then analyse itsminimal SU(2) and SU(3) realisations and study their phenomenology, and show that theirreducible dark radiation they predict is the sharpest test of the construction in the lightof recent updated experimental constraints. Finally, we ask how such a hidden sector coulddevelop a vector portal, or kinetic mixing, with the visible sector without breaking the purelyhidden structure, and compute the minimal contribution that does so.

arxiv:2610.05377.title: Exploring anomaly-free dark photon models through solar neutrino-electron scattering in ton-scale dark matter detectors
arxiv:2610.05377.abstract: We study the phenomenological implications of anomaly-free dark photon models using low-energy solar neutrino-electron elastic scattering data from the ton-scale PandaX-4T and XENONnT experiments. Focusing on U ( 1 ) X gauge extensions that incorporate both kinetic and mass mixing, we derive novel exclusion limits across the parameter spaces of six benchmark models. Our analysis demonstrates that the stringency of these limits is directly correlated with the theoretical leptonic charge assignments of the respective models. Additionally, we provide model-independent limits by isolating the pure kinetic and pure mass mixing scenarios. In the sub-MeV mediator mass regime, our results meaningfully improve upon existing limits from previous neutrino-electron scattering experiments, such as CHARM-II, TEXONO, and GEMMA. Ultimately, these findings yield improved limits on low-mass dark photon models, demonstrating their complementarity with other ventures in the global search for dark portals.

arxiv:2609.40237.title: First double-differential cross-section measurements in proton multiplicity and kinematics for mesonless $ν_μ$ charged-current interactions on argon using the MicroBooNE detector
arxiv:2609.40237.abstract: We present the first double-differential cross-section measurements of muon neutrino charged-current interactions on argon with no mesons and one or more protons ($N_{p} \geq 1$) in the final state as a function of proton multiplicity and kinematics. The analysis uses the full Booster Neutrino Beam dataset collected by the MicroBooNE detector at Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory, corresponding to a total of $1.30 \times 10^{21}$ protons on target. We measure cross sections as a function of the proton multiplicity, the momenta and muon-proton opening angles of the leading and subleading protons up to and including the fourth-leading proton, as well as the total available kinetic energy of the hadronic system. The treatment of the statistical and systematic uncertainties includes correlations between the different extracted distributions. The measured cross sections are compared to predictions from several event generators using different primary and final-state interaction models. The results reveal strong sensitivity to the modeling of final-state interactions, and none of the generators tested provides a fully adequate description of the data. Significant disagreement between data and predictions is observed in the proton multiplicity distributions, particularly at backward opening angles and for subleading proton kinematics.

arxiv:2609.37895.title: Measurement of Neutrino Oscillation Parameters at JUNO and Indication of the Neutrino Mass Ordering
arxiv:2609.37895.abstract: We report an improved measurement of neutrino oscillation parameters at the Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory (JUNO) and the consequent indication of neutrino mass ordering. The analysis is based on 207.2 live days of data, comprising 8,294 inverse beta-decay candidates collected at an average reactor baseline of 52.5 km. A world-leading precision of approximately 1% was achieved for the atmospheric neutrino mass splitting $Δm^2_{31}$, with $Δm^2_{31}=+2.509^{+0.027}_{-0.025}\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{eV}^2$ for normal ordering and $Δm^2_{31}=-2.482^{+0.025}_{-0.026}\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{eV}^2$ for inverted ordering, using the Daya Bay constraint in the fit to resolve the correct physical minimum under each mass-ordering hypothesis. We further improved the world's most precise measurements of the solar oscillation parameters, obtaining $\sin^2θ_{12}=0.3036\pm0.0064$ and $Δm^2_{21}=(7.388\pm0.078)\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm{eV}^2$, corresponding to relative precisions of 2.1% and 1.1%, respectively. Incorporating constraints on $Δm^2_{31}$ from long-baseline accelerator neutrino experiments into our analysis favored normal ordering over inverted ordering, with a one-sided significance of at least $2.1σ$ across all possible CP-violating phases; a Bayesian analysis yielded a Bayes factor of 10.18 in favor of normal ordering.
authors: de André, João Pedro Athay de Marcondes

arxiv:2609.34324.title: Relic Neutrinos Probing Small Scale Primordial Non-Gaussianity
arxiv:2609.34324.abstract: Relic neutrinos retain a record of electromagnetic entropy production after neutrino decoupling, probing primordial modes erased from the primary CMB. We derive the cubic photon number source from acoustic damping and its leading folded sensitive bispectrum window, with neutrino decoupling, thermalization, and acoustic coherence combined in a single response kernel. For excited initial states, this kernel filters the physical folded profile and yields a sharpness dependent transmission condition, directly connecting small scale primordial non-Gaussianity to relic neutrino capture rates.

arxiv:2609.36005.title: Stochastic gravitational-wave background from subsolar neutron stars in collapsar disks
arxiv:2609.36005.abstract: The fragmentation of the neutrino-cooled accretion disks that surround the black holes formed in collapsars has recently been proposed as an astrophysical channel for the production of neutron stars with masses well below the standard core-collapse floor. These disk-born objects merge either with one another or with the central black hole, and the superposition of all such mergers across cosmic history sources a stochastic gravitational-wave background. In this work we compute the energy density of this background for both merger channels, adopting a formation history tied to the observed rate of long gamma-ray bursts. We find that the merger of a subsolar neutron star with the central black hole is the loudest channel, already constrained by current data and within reach of next-generation observatories, while the binary neutron-star channel is at most two orders of magnitude fainter, with its widest binaries remaining accessible to next-generation detectors. Confronting these predictions with the fourth observing run of the LIGO--Virgo--KAGRA Collaboration, we derive two upper bounds on the fraction of collapsars whose disks produce such mergers: a robust one from the non-detection of an isotropic background, and a tighter one that could be achieved by a dedicated search for resolvable subsolar events in current data. Gravitational waves from non-axisymmetric deformations of the collapsar disk itself would provide an additional independent signature for the collapsar scenario, enabling cross-correlation studies with future deci-Hz detectors. Overall, the background computed here provides a population-level probe of disk-born subsolar neutron stars, which next-generation detectors could bring firmly into view.

arxiv:2609.30990.title: Teukolsky Master Equation for a Kerr-like metric with Mass Quadrupole Moment
arxiv:2609.30990.abstract: The Teukolsky Master Equation (TME) is a powerful technique used to study perturbations of a spacetime with gravitational, electromagnetic, and neutrino components. The well-known Kerr metric is a suitable candidate for this formalism because it is a Petrov type D metric. However, the Kerr metric represents the exterior spacetime of a perfect sphere and only black holes are described using this metric. For another astrophysical object, such as fast-spinning neutron stars, the Kerr metric is not valid due to the rotation induced deformations to the gravitational source. The main goal of the present work is to show a TME for a Kerr-like metric (KL) with a mass quadrupole moment parameter $q$. This new parameter will represent deformations from a perfect sphere; therefore, KL is a better candidate to study perturbations surrounding spinning stars.

arxiv:2609.31833.title: Neutrino Direct Simulation Monte Carlo: Accurate modeling of out-of-equilibrium decaying cosmological relics
arxiv:2609.31833.abstract: We consider nonstandard cosmologies in which decaying relics inject energy at MeV temperatures, driving neutrinos out of equilibrium. The subsequent neutrino evolution shapes predictions for the cosmic radiation density and primordial light element abundances. Earlier work introduced Neutrino Direct Simulation Monte Carlo ($ν$DSMC), which describes neutrino transport through Monte Carlo sampling of particle interactions. Here, we extend this method by jointly evolving the relic population, neutrino spectra, electromagnetic plasma, and cosmic expansion, and coupling this evolution to Big Bang nucleosynthesis. The framework includes direct and inverse decays of the relic, neutrino flavor conversion, quantum statistics, and pion production by energetic neutrinos. To reveal the physical impact of these effects and independently test $ν$DSMC, we compare several approaches to neutrino evolution across a range of nonstandard cosmological scenarios. We find excellent agreement with independent solutions of quantum kinetic or quasi-classical Boltzmann equations. Compared with these calculations, $ν$DSMC includes a broader range of physical processes and is substantially faster for strongly nonthermal neutrino populations. This makes broad, robust parameter scans for nonstandard cosmologies practical. We show that when departures from thermal equilibrium are large, approximations that average over neutrino momenta can give qualitatively incorrect predictions, including the wrong sign of the change in the effective number of neutrino species and substantially incorrect primordial nuclear abundances. We conclude that the extended $ν$DSMC framework enables reliable cosmological tests of new physics by following neutrino thermalization and its observable consequences.

arxiv:2609.29761.title: Multi-messenger and multi-band signal from first-order phase transitions in proto-neutron stars
arxiv:2609.29761.abstract: A first-order phase transition (PT) alters a compact star on two scales: globally, via growth of a quark-matter core, and microscopically, via collision of quark bubbles, driving a simultaneous gravitational-wave (GW) emission in the kHz and MHz bands. Using a constrained ensemble of model-agnostic equations of state, we follow the accretion-driven evolution of proto-neutron stars through the PT and compute the resulting multi-band GW signal. The correlations found between the kHz emission and the MHz burst could help constrain nuclear matter and the physics of the PT. A delayed neutrino burst should accompany the signal, with the delay set by the details of the PT, thus providing a prime multi-messenger source.

arxiv:2609.28334.title: Nested disappearing-track plus displaced-vertex topology at the HL-LHC: a dual long-lived-particle signature of the scotogenic model
arxiv:2609.28334.abstract: The scotogenic model generates sub-eV neutrino masses radiatively through small Yukawa couplings $\sim \mathcal {O}(10^{-3})$ that also set the decay length of the heavy neutral fermion $N_2$; in the compressed regime a separate, much smaller Yukawa entry $\sim \mathcal {O}(10^{-6})$ additionally renders the charged scalar $\tilde{\eta }^{\pm }$ long-lived. We study the compressed-spectrum regime of its two-inert-doublet variant ($\varDelta M_{\textrm{comp}}= m_{\tilde{\eta }^\pm }- m_{N_2}\simeq 200\,\text {MeV}$), in which small Yukawa entries render both the charged scalar $\tilde{\eta }^{\pm }$ and the heavy neutral fermion $N_2$ long-lived and produce a nested cascade at the High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC): $\tilde{\eta }^{\pm }$ leaves a disappearing track (DT), decays to an invisible $N_2$, which travels macroscopically before forming a displaced dilepton vertex (DV). The two slow flights combine into a 4D time-of-flight delay $\varDelta t\sim 200$-$800\,\text {ps}$ resolvable by the CMS MIP Timing Detector, while the DT-to-DV displacement vector inherits the parent track direction, yielding a spatial back-pointing correlation with no SM analogue. These two handles are expected to suppress the background to $B\sim 10^{-5}$-$10^{-3}$ events, and the discovery remains $5\sigma $-significant for any background up to $B\sim 10$ events. At the benchmark ($m_{N_2}=150\,\text {GeV}$ and proper decay lengths $c\tau _{\tilde{\eta }^\pm }=300\,\text {mm}$, $c\tau _{N_2}=189\,\text {mm}$) the strategy yields $N_s\approx 1212$ signal events at $3000\,\text {fb}^{-1}$ and establishes sensitivity across $15\,\text {mm}\lesssim c\tau _{\tilde{\eta }^\pm }\lesssim 300\,\text {mm}$, $10\,\text {mm}\lesssim c\tau _{N_2}\lesssim 1000\,\text {mm}$, a correlated region left uncovered by any standalone DT or DV search. Because the $N_2$ decay length is controlled by the same Yukawa couplings that generate sub-eV neutrino masses, mapping this nested cascade turns the HL-LHC into a direct collider probe of the interaction responsible for neutrino mass.

arxiv:2609.24796.title: Goodness-of-fit for multi-distribution neutrino cross-section measurements with shared events
arxiv:2609.24796.abstract: When multiple differential cross-section measurements are extracted from a common event sample, the same events contribute simultaneously to multiple distributions. This event-sharing structure imposes exact linear constraints among the bin counts, reducing the effective dimensionality of the measurement below the total number of bins. Since the covariance matrix obeys these inter-distribution constraints, it contains a rank deficiency. While limited numerical precision may inadvertently restore invertibility, the $χ^{2}$ contributions along constrained dimensions will be arbitrary, yielding unphysically inflated $χ^{2}$ values in global goodness-of-fit tests. We present the range-projected $χ^{2}$, a test statistic that restricts the goodness-of-fit test to the subspace carrying independent statistical information, yielding a $χ^{2}$ with $N_\text{bins} - N_\text{null}$ degrees of freedom, where $N_\text{null}$ is the number of independent constraints. We show that this rank deficiency is a predictable consequence of the event-sharing structure, and that $N_\text{null}$ decomposes into a structural contribution determined a priori from the binning geometry and a kinematic contribution that depends on the phase-space occupancy. The method is validated with an analytical toy model and a simulated neutrino--argon cross-section measurement including unfolding and multi-source systematic uncertainties.

arxiv:2609.20552.title: Mineral Detection of Neutrinos and Dark Matter 2026 Proceedings
arxiv:2609.20552.abstract: The fourth "Mineral Detection of Neutrinos and Dark Matter" (MDvDM'26) meeting was held April 14-17, 2026 in Karlsruhe, Germany, hosted by the Institute for Astroparticle Physics (IAP) at Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT). These proceedings detail the contributions that were presented during MDvDM'26, illustrating the unprecedented progress in theoretical, computational and experimental studies towards the realization of the concept of mineral detectors. Mineral detectors represent an emerging particle detection concept that has risen in prominence in recent years due to the advent of modern computational and high-resolution microscopy techniques. Natural and synthetic crystals are capable of retaining microscopic damage features induced by nuclear recoils, which could be then read out with a variety of micrometer and nanometer resolution microscopy techniques. On laboratory time scales mineral detectors could be employed for reactor neutrino monitoring and dark matter detection, with the potential to measure the directions as well as the energies of the induced nuclear recoils. Uniquely, ancient natural crystals (so-called paleo-detectors) that have been recording nuclear recoils over geological timescales could be used for studying astrophysical neutrinos, cosmic rays, dark matter and heavy exotic particles, as well as the variation of their fluxes over our Galaxy's lifetime. In recent years the international MDvDM community has been successfully tackling the challenges associated with realizing the concept of mineral detectors, opening the pathway towards a fully fledged experimental program and potential future discoveries.

arxiv:2609.20936.title: AutoTherm: Automated Thermal Field Theory rates for cosmology
arxiv:2609.20936.abstract: AutoTherm is a modular code automating the determination of thermal production and interaction rates for cosmology from Thermal Field Theory. This first release computes fully automatically the leading-order contribution from ultrarelativistic $2\leftrightarrow 2$ processes to the production rate of an off-equilibrium $\vartheta$ particle coupled to a thermal bath. It takes as input a FeynRules model file describing the Lagrangian of the bath-$\vartheta$ system. The AutoTherm program consists of a Wolfram package, which utilises FeynArts/FormCalc, together with a few Python modules for symbolic and numerical routines. Their combined usage leads from the model file to the rate, but each component can also be used in a standalone manner. The main strength of this release is the automated, model-independent handling of Hard Thermal Loop resummation, which is necessary whenever a $2\leftrightarrow 2$ process is mediated by a $t$-channel massless mediator. Developments in Thermal Field Theory reduce the apparently large model dependence to the determination of the thermal mass of the mediator, which we automate successfully. They further allow us to provide three leading-order-equivalent implementations of HTL resummation. Their spread provides a first estimate of the theory uncertainty from higher-order thermal corrections. We showcase the strength of our AutoTherm framework by successfully reproducing or correcting a host of results in the literature, such as the thermal production rate of ultrarelativistic right-handed neutrinos, of gravitons and gravitinos, of axions and of dark photons.

arxiv:2609.20949.title: First Measurement of Differential Cross Sections in Kinematic Imbalance Variables with Electron Neutrino Interactions Using the MicroBooNE Detector
arxiv:2609.20949.abstract: We report the first measurement of flux-integrated cross sections as a function of kinematic imbalance variables for electron neutrino interactions on argon. Kinematic imbalance variables, applied here to electron neutrino interactions for the first time, are particularly interesting due to their sensitivity to effects such as Fermi motion, multinucleon processes, and final-state interactions, providing a detailed lens to study neutrino-nucleus interactions.
